body.text: Śālistambasūtram |

evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣusahasraiḥ saṃbahulaiśca bodhisattvamahāsattvaiḥ | athāyuṣmān śāriputro yena maitreyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya caṃkramaḥ, tenopasamakramīt | upasaṃkramya anyonyaṃ saṃmodanīyāṃ kathāṃ bahuvidhāṃ vyatisārayitvā ubhau śilātale upāviśatām ||

athāyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - adyātra śālistambamavalokya maitreya bhagavatā bhikṣubhyaḥ sūtramidamuktam - yo bhikṣavaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati, sa dharmaṃ paśyati | yo dharmaṃ paśyati, sa buddhaṃ paśyati | ityuktvā bhagavāṃstūṣṇīṃ babhūvaṃ | atha maitreya sugatoktasūtrāntasya arthaḥ katamaḥ? pratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaḥ? dharma katamaḥ? buddhaḥ katamaḥ? kathaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyan dharmaṃ paśyati? kathaṃ dharmaṃ paśyan buddhaṃ paśyati?

evamukte maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ āyuṣmantaṃ śāradvatīputrametadavocat - atra yaduktaṃ bhadanta śāriputra bhagavatā dharmasvāminā sarvajñena - yo bhikṣavaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati, sa dharmaṃ paśyati | yo dharmaṃ paśyati, sa buddhaṃ paśyati iti, tatra katamaḥ pratītyasamutpādo nāma? pratītyasamutpādo nāma yadidam - asmin sati idaṃ bhavati, asyotpādādidamutpadyate | yaduta avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ | saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam | vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam | nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam | ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ | sparśapratyayā vedanā | vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā | tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam | upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ | bhavapratyayā jāti | jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | tatra avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ | saṃskāranirodhādvijñānanirodhaḥ | vijñānanirodhānnāmarūpanirodhaḥ | nāmarūpanirodhāt ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ | ṣaḍāyatananirodhāt sparśanirodhaḥ | sparśanirodhāt vedanānirodhaḥ | vedanānirodhāt tṛṣṇānirodhaḥ | tṛṣṇānirodhādupādānanirodhaḥ | upādānanirodhādbhavanirodhaḥ | bhavanirodhājjātinirodhaḥ | jātinirodhājjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati | ayamucyate pratītyasamutpādo bhagavatā ||

katamo dharmaḥ? āryāṣṭāṅgiko mārgaḥ | tadyathā - samyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ samyagvāk samyakkarmāntaḥ samyagājīvaḥ samyagvyāyāmaḥ samyaksmṛtiḥ samyaksamādhiḥ | ayamukto bhagavatā āryāṣṭāṅgiko mārgaḥ phalalābhanirvāṇaikasaṃgṛhīto dharmaḥ ||
tatra katamo buddho bhagavān? yaḥ sarvadharmāvabodhādbuddha ucyate, sa āryaprajñānetraḥ dharmakāyasamanvitaḥ śaikṣāśaikṣadharmānimān paśyati ||

tatra kathaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyati? ihoktaṃ bhagavatā - ya imaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ satatasamitam, ajīvaṃ nirjīvaṃ yathāvadaviparītamajātamabhūtamakṛtamasaṃskṛtamapratighamanālambanaṃ śivamabhayamanāhāryamavyayamavyupaśamasvabhāvaṃ paśyati, (sa dharmaṃ paśyati) | yastu evaṃ dharmaṃ (

children.text: ) satatasamitamajīvaṃ nirjīvaṃ yathāvadaviparītamajātamabhūtamakṛtamasaṃskṛtamapratighamanālambanaṃ śivamanāhāryamavyayamavyupaśamasvabhāvaṃ paśyati, so 'nuttaradharmaśarīraṃ buddhaṃ paśyati | āryadharmābhisamaye samyagjñānopanayenaiva ||
children.translated_text: continuously and constantly, without life-force (<s>ajīva</s>), without a soul (<s>nirjīva</s>), as it truly is, without error, unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), without obstruction, without support, quiescent, indestructible, imperishable, of the nature of cessation — he sees the <s>Buddha</s> as the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-body. Through the realization of the noble <s>Dharma</s>, by the approach of right knowledge alone.

body.text: pratītyasamutpāda iti kasmāducyate? sahetukaḥ sapratyayo nāhetuko nāpratyayaḥ, tasmāt pratītyasamutpāda ityucyate | tatra bhagavatā pratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇaṃ saṃkṣepeṇoktamidaṃpratyayatāphalam | utpādādvā tathāgatānāmanutpādādvā sthitaiveṣā dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā yāvadyaiṣā dharmatā dharmasthititā dharmaniyāmatā pratītyasamutpādasamatā tathatā aviparītatathatā ananyatathatā bhūtatā satyatā aviparītatā aviparyayatā iti ||
body.translated_text: Why is it called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)? Because it arises with causes and with conditions, not without causes and not without conditions — therefore it is called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>. In this regard, the Blessed One stated the characteristic of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> in brief as the fruit of conditionality: 'Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, this nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>) stands firm — namely, this <s>dharmatā</s>, the stability of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasthititā</s>), the regularity of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaniyāmatā</s>), the equality of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpādasamatā</s>), suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), non-erroneous suchness (<s>aviparītatathatā</s>), non-other suchness (<s>ananyatathatā</s>), reality (<s>bhūtatā</s>), truth (<s>satyatā</s>), non-erroneousness (<s>aviparītatā</s>), non-reversal (<s>aviparyayatā</s>).'

body.text: atha ca punarayaṃ pratītyasamutpādo dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate | katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām? yadidaṃ hetūpanibandhataḥ pratyayopanibandhataśca | so 'pi dvividho draṣṭavyaḥ - bāhyaśca ādhyātmikaśca | tatra bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandhaḥ katamāḥ? yadidaṃ bījādaṅkuraḥ | aṅkurātpatram | patrātkāṇḍam | kāṇḍānnālam | nālādgaṇḍaḥ | gaṇḍādgarbham | garbhācchūkaḥ | śūkātpuṣpam | puṣpāt phalam | asati bīje aṅkuro na bhavati, yāvadasati puṣpe phalaṃ na bhavati | sati tu bīje aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati, evaṃ yāvat sati puṣpe phalasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | tatra bījasya naivaṃ bhavati - ahamaṅkuramabhinirvartayāmīti | aṅkurasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bījenābhinirvartita iti | evaṃ yāvat puṣpasya naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ phalamabhinirvartayāmīti | phalasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ puṣpeṇābhinirvartitamiti | atha punaḥ bīje sati aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati prādurbhāvaḥ | evaṃ yāvat puṣpe sati phalasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati prādurbhāvaḥ | evaṃ bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And furthermore, this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> arises from two kinds of causes. Which two? Namely, from the connection of the causal factor (<s>hetūpanibandha</s>) and from the connection of the conditional factor (<s>pratyayopanibandha</s>). And it should be seen as twofold: external and internal (<s>ādhyātmika</s>). Regarding this, what is the causal connection of external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>? From the seed comes the sprout; from the sprout, the leaf; from the leaf, the stem; from the stem, the stalk; from the stalk, the bud; from the bud, the calyx; from the calyx, the awn; from the awn, the flower; from the flower, the fruit. When there is no seed, the sprout does not come into being; likewise, when there is no flower, the fruit does not come into being. But when there is a seed, the production of the sprout occurs; similarly, when there is a flower, the production of the fruit occurs. In this regard, the seed does not think: 'I produce the sprout.' Nor does the sprout think: 'I have been produced by the seed.' Similarly, the flower does not think: 'I produce the fruit.' Nor does the fruit think: 'I have been produced by the flower.' Yet when there is a seed, the production and manifestation of the sprout occurs. Similarly, when there is a flower, the production and manifestation of the fruit occurs. Thus should the causal connection of external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> be understood.

body.text: kathaṃ bāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ? ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnā samudāyāt | katameṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ samavāyāt? yadidaṃ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśaṛtudhātusamavāyādbāhyasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | tatra pṛthivīdhāturbījasya saṃdhāraṇakṛtyaṃ karoti | abdhāturbījaṃ snehayati | tejodhāturbījaṃ paripācayati | vāyudhāturbījamabhinirharati | ākāśadhāturbījasyānāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karotīti | ṛturapi bījasya pariṇāmanākṛtyaṃ karoti | asatsu eṣu pratyayeṣu bījādaṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirna bhavati | yadā bāhyaśca pṛthivīdhāturavikalo bhavati, evamaptejovāyvākāśaṛtudhātavaścāvikalā bhavanti, tataḥ savaṣāṃ samavāyādbīje nirudhyamāne aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | tatra pṛthivīdhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bījasya saṃdhāraṇakṛtyaṃ karomḥti | evamabdhātorapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bḥjaṃ snehayāmḥti | tejodhātorapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bḥjaṃ paripācayāmḥti | vāyudhātorapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bḥjamabhinirharāmḥti | ākāśadhātorapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bḥjasyānāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karomḥti | ṛtorapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bḥjasya pariṇāmanākṛtyaṃ karomḥti | bḥjasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ bḥjaṃ (aṅkuraṃ?) abhinirvartayāmḥti | aṅkurasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayairabhi

children.text: ) iti | atha punaḥ satsu eteṣu pratyayeṣu bḥje nirudhyamāne aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttiebhavati | evaṃ yāvat puṣpe sati phalasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | sa ca aṅkuro na svayaṃkṛto na parakṛto nobhayakṛto neśvarakṛto na kālapariṇāmito na prakṛtisaṃbhūto (na caikakāraṇādhḥno) nāpyahetusamutpannaḥ | atha punaḥ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśaṛtudhātusamavāyād bḥje nirudhyamāne aṅkurasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | evaṃ bāhyasya pratḥtyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) Thus. Now again, when these conditions are present and the seed perishes, the arising of the sprout occurs. Likewise, up to: when the flower is present, the arising of the fruit occurs. And that sprout is not self-made, not other-made, not made by both, not made by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), not transformed by time, not produced from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), not dependent on a single cause, nor arisen without cause. Yet, from the confluence of earth, water, fire, wind, space, season, and element, when the seed perishes, the arising of the sprout occurs. Thus should the conditional linkage of external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) be understood.

body.translated_text: How should the conditional connection of external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> be understood? From the coming together of six elements. From the coming together of which six? The conditional connection of external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> should be understood from the coming together of the earth element, water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and the season element. In this regard, the earth element performs the function of supporting the seed; the water element moistens the seed; the fire element ripens the seed; the wind element draws forth the seed; the space element performs the function of not obstructing the seed; and the season performs the function of transforming the seed. When these conditions are absent, the production of the sprout from the seed does not occur. But when the external earth element is complete, and likewise the water, fire, wind, space, and season elements are complete, then from the coming together of all of them, as the seed ceases, the production of the sprout occurs. In this regard, the earth element does not think: 'I perform the function of supporting the seed.' Likewise the water element does not think: 'I moisten the seed.' The fire element does not think: 'I ripen the seed.' The wind element does not think: 'I draw forth the seed.' The space element does not think: 'I perform the function of not obstructing the seed.' The season does not think: 'I perform the function of transforming the seed.' The seed does not think: 'I produce the sprout.' The sprout does not think: 'I have been produced by these conditions'

body.text: tatra bāhyaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhirākārairdraṣṭavyaḥ | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? na śāśvatataḥ, nocchedataḥ, na saṃkrāntitaḥ, parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ, tatsadṛśānuprabandhataśca | kathaṃ na śāśvatata iti? yasmādanyo 'ṅkuraḥ anyadbījam | na ca ya evāṅkuraḥ tadeva bījam | na ca niruddhādbījādaṅkura utpadyate nāpyaniruddhāt | bījaṃ punarnirudhyate, tadaivāṅkuraścotpadyate | tasmānna śāśvatataḥ | kathaṃ nocchedataḥ? na ca pūrvaniruddhād bījādaṅkuro niṣpadyate | nāpyaniruddhāt | api ca bījaṃ ca nirudhyate, tasminneva samaye aṅkura utpadyate tulādaṇḍonnāmāvanāmavat | ato nocchedataḥ || kathaṃ na saṃkrāntitaḥ? visadṛśo bījādaṅkura iti | ato na saṃkrāntitaḥ || kathaṃ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ? parīttaṃ bījamupyate, vipulaphalamabhinirvartayatīti | ataḥ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ || kathaṃ tatsadṛśānuprabandhataḥ? yādṛśaṃ bījamupyate, tādṛśaṃ phalamabhinirvartayatīti | atastatsadṛśānuprabandhataśceti || evaṃ bāhyaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhirākārairdraṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be viewed in five aspects. Which five? Not as eternal, not as annihilated, not as transferred, as producing an abundant fruit from a small cause, and as continuity of what is similar to that. How is it not eternal? Because the sprout is one thing and the seed another. It is not the case that the sprout itself is the seed. Nor does the sprout arise from a seed that has [already] perished, nor from one that has not perished. Rather, the seed perishes and at that very moment the sprout arises. Therefore, it is not eternal. How is it not annihilated? The sprout is not produced from a seed that has previously perished, nor from one that has not perished. Rather, the seed perishes, and at that very moment the sprout arises—like the rising and falling of the arms of a balance. Therefore, it is not annihilated. How is it not transferred? Because the sprout is dissimilar from the seed. Therefore, it is not transferred. How does an abundant fruit arise from a small cause? A small seed is sown, and it produces an abundant fruit. Therefore, an abundant fruit arises from a small cause. How is there continuity of what is similar to that? Whatever kind of seed is sown, that kind of fruit it produces. Therefore, there is continuity of what is similar to that. Thus, external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) should be viewed in five aspects.

body.text: evamādhyātmiko 'pi pratītyasamutpādo dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate | katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām? yadidaṃ hetūpanibandhataḥ pratyayopanibandhataśca | tatrādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandhaḥ katamaḥ? yadidamavidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, yāvajjātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamiti | avidyā cennābhaviṣyat, naiva saṃskārāḥ prajñāsyante | evaṃ yāvajjātiścennābhaviṣyat, jarāmaraṇaṃ na prajñāsyate | atha satyāmavidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇāmabhinirvṛttirbhavati | evaṃ yāvajjātyāṃ sattyāṃ jarāmaraṇasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | tatra avidyāyā naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ saṃskārānabhinirvartayāmīti | saṃskārāṇāmapi naivaṃ bhavati - vayamavidyayā abhinirvatitā iti | evaṃ yāvajjāterapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ jarāmaraṇamabhinirvartayāmīti | jarāmaraṇasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ jātyābhinirvartitamiti | atha ca satyāmavidyāyāṃ saṃskārāṇāmabhinirvṛttirbhavati prādurbhāvaḥ | evaṃ yāvajjātyāṃ satyāṃ jarāmaraṇasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati prādurbhāvaḥ | evamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya hetūpanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) too arises from two causes. Which two? Namely, from the linkage of causes (<s>hetu</s>) and from the linkage of conditions (<s>pratyaya</s>). Therein, what is the causal linkage of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>? Namely: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), up to: conditioned by <s>jāti</s> (birth) arise <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death). If <s>avidyā</s> did not exist, <s>saṃskāras</s> would not be known at all. Likewise, up to: if <s>jāti</s> did not exist, <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> would not be known. But when <s>avidyā</s> is present, the arising of <s>saṃskāras</s> occurs. Likewise, up to: when <s>jāti</s> is present, the arising of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> occurs. Therein, <s>avidyā</s> does not think thus: 'I produce the <s>saṃskāras</s>.' Nor do the <s>saṃskāras</s> think thus: 'We are produced by <s>avidyā</s>.' Likewise, up to: <s>jāti</s> does not think thus: 'I produce <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>.' Nor does <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> think thus: 'I am produced by <s>jāti</s>.' Yet when <s>avidyā</s> is present, the arising and manifestation of <s>saṃskāras</s> occurs. Likewise, up to: when <s>jāti</s> is present, the arising and manifestation of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> occurs. Thus should the causal linkage of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) be understood.

body.text: kathamādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ? ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt | katameṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāṃ samavāyāt? yadidaṃ pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśavijñānadhātūnāṃ samavāyādādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ | tatra ādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ? yo 'yaṃ kāyasya saṃśleṣataḥ kaṭhinabhāvamabhinirvartayati, ayamucyate pṛthivīdhātuḥ | yaḥ kāyasya anuparigrahakṛtyaṃ karoti, ayamucyate 'bdhātuḥ | yaṃ kāyasya aśitapītabhakṣitaṃ paripācayati, (

children.text: ) ayamucyate tejodhātuḥ | yaṃ kāyasya āśvāsapraśvāsakṛtyaṃ karoti, ayamucyate vāyudhātuḥ | yaṃ kāyasyāntaḥśauṣiryamabhinirvartayati, ayamucyate ākāśadhātuḥ | ya kāyasya nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati, naḍakalāpayogena, pañcavijñānakāyasaṃyuktaṃ sāsravaṃ ca manovijñānam, ayamucyate vijñānadhātuḥ | tatra asatāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ kāyasyotpattirnaṃ bhavati | yadā ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivīdhāturavikalo bhavati, evamaptejovāyvākāśavijñānadhātavaśca avikalā bhavanti, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ samavāyāt kāyasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati | tatra pṛthivīdhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasya saṃśleṣataḥ kaṭhinabhāvamabhinirvartayāmīti | abdhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasya anuparigrahakṛtyaṃ karomīti | tejodhātorapi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasya aśitapītabhakṣitaṃ paripācayāmīti | vāyudhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasya āśvāsapraśvāsakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ākāśadhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasyāntaḥśauṣiryamabhinirvartayāmīti | vijñānadhātornaivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ kāyasya nāmarūpamabhinirvartayāmīti | kāyasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanita iti | atha ca satsu eṣu pratyayeṣu kāyasyotpattirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: ) this is called the fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>). That which performs the function of inhalation and exhalation in the body — this is called the wind element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>). That which produces the internal hollowness of the body — this is called the space element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>). That which produces the sprout of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) in the body, connected with the five groups of consciousness in the manner of a bundle of reeds, together with the defiled mental consciousness — this is called the consciousness element (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>). When these conditions are absent, the arising of the body does not occur. When the internal earth element is complete, and likewise the water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness elements are also complete, then from the coming together of all of them, the production of the body occurs. Therein, the earth element does not think: 'I produce the quality of hardness through the cohesion of the body.' The water element does not think: 'I perform the function of holding the body together.' The fire element too does not think: 'I digest what is eaten, drunk, and consumed in the body.' The wind element does not think: 'I perform the function of inhalation and exhalation in the body.' The space element does not think: 'I produce the internal hollowness of the body.' The consciousness element does not think: 'I produce the name-and-form of the body.' The body too does not think: 'I am produced by these conditions.' And yet, when these conditions are present, the arising of the body occurs.

body.translated_text: How should the conditional linkage of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) be understood? From the confluence of six <s>dhātus</s> (elements). From the confluence of which six <s>dhātus</s>? Namely, from the confluence of the <s>dhātus</s> of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness should the conditional linkage of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> be understood. Therein, what is the earth element of internal <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>? That which produces the quality of hardness from the cohesion of the body—this is called the earth element. That which performs the function of holding the body together—this is called the water element. That which digests what is eaten, drunk, and consumed by the body,

body.text: tatra pṛthivīdhāturnātmā na sattvo na jīvo na jantuḥ na manajo na mānavo na strī na pumān na napuṃsakaṃ na cāhaṃ na mama na cānyasya kasyacit | evamabdhātustejodhāturvāyudhāturākāśadhāturvijñānadhātuḥ nātmā na sattvo na jīvo na jantuḥ na manujo na mānavo na strī na pumān na napuṃsakaṃ na cāhaṃ na mama na cānyasya kasyacit ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the earth element is not a self, not a being, not a life-force, not a creature, not a human, not a person, not a woman, not a man, not a neuter, not 'I,' not 'mine,' nor belonging to anyone else. Likewise, the water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element are not a self, not a being, not a life-force, not a creature, not a human, not a person, not a woman, not a man, not a neuter, not 'I,' not 'mine,' nor belonging to anyone else.

body.text: tatra avidyā katamā? yā eṣāmeva ṣaṇṇāṃ dhātūnāmekasaṃjñā piṇḍasaṃjñā nityasaṃjñā dhruvasaṃjñā śāśvatasaṃjñā sukhasaṃjñā ātmasaṃjñā sattvajīvajantupoṣapuruṣapudgalasaṃjñā manujamānavasaṃjñā ahaṃkāramamakārasaṃjñā, evamādi vividhamajñānam | iyamucyate avidyeti | evamavidyāyāṃ satyāṃ viṣayeṣu rāgadveṣamohāḥ pravartante | tatra ye rāgadveṣamohā viṣayeṣu, amī(avidyāpratyayāḥ) saṃskārā ityucyante | vastuprativijñaptirvijñānam | vijñānasahabhuvaścatvāraḥ skandhā arūpiṇaḥ upādānākhyāḥ tannāma | rūpaṃ catvāri mahābhūtāni tāni copādāya rūpam | tacca nāma tacca rūpamaikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya tannāmarūpam | nāmarūpasaṃniśritāni indriyāṇi ṣaḍāyatanam | trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṃnipātaḥ sparśaḥ | sparśānubhavo vedanā | vedanādhyavasānaṃ tṛṣṇā | tṛṣṇāvaipulyamupādānam | upādānanirjātaṃ punarbhavajanakaṃ karma bhavaḥ | bhavahetukaḥ skandhaprādurbhāvo jātiḥ | jātasya skandhaparipāko jarā | jīrṇasya skandhasya vināśo maraṇam | mriyamāṇasya saṃmūḍhasya sābhiṣvaṅgasya antaḥparidāhaḥ śokaḥ | śokotthamālapanaṃ paridevaḥ | pañcavijñānakāyasaṃyuktamasātamanubhavanaṃ duḥkham | manasikārasaṃyuktaṃ mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ daurmanasyam | ye cāpi anye evamādayaḥ kleśāḥ, te upāyāsā iti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>)? It is the perception of these very six elements as a unity, as a mass, as permanent, as stable, as eternal, as pleasurable, as a self, as a being, a life-force, a creature, a nourisher, a person, an individual, as human, as person, as 'I-making' and 'mine-making' — such varied forms of ignorance. This is called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). When ignorance is thus present, attachment, aversion, and delusion arise toward objects. Therein, the attachment, aversion, and delusion toward objects — these, [having ignorance as their condition,] are called <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). The cognition that apprehends an object is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). The four formless <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) that co-arise with consciousness, called <s>upādāna</s> (clinging-aggregates) — that is <s>nāma</s> (name). Form (<s>rūpa</s>) is the four great elements and the form derived from them. Combining that name and that form together — that is <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). The sense faculties dependent on name-and-form are the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>). The coming together of three <s>dharmas</s> is contact (<s>sparśa</s>). The experience of contact is feeling (<s>vedanā</s>). The fixation upon feeling is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). The intensification of craving is clinging (<s>upādāna</s>). The <s>karma</s> (action) produced by clinging that generates renewed existence is becoming (<s>bhava</s>). The manifestation of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) caused by becoming is birth (<s>jāti</s>). The maturation of the aggregates of what has been born is aging (<s>jarā</s>). The destruction of the aged aggregates is death (<s>maraṇa</s>). The internal burning of one who is dying, who is confused and clinging — that is grief (<s>śoka</s>). The lamentation arising from grief is wailing (<s>parideva</s>). The unpleasant experience connected with the five groups of consciousness is suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). The mental suffering connected with mental attention is distress (<s>daurmanasya</s>). And whatever other afflictions of this kind — those are anguish (<s>upāyāsa</s>).

body.text: tatra mahāndhakārārthena avidyā | abhisaṃskārārthena saṃskārāḥ | vijñāpanārthena vijñānam | anyonyopastambhanārthena nāmarūpam | āyadvārārthena ṣaḍāyatanam | sparśanārthena sparśaḥ | anubhavanārthena vedanā | paritarṣaṇārthena tṛṣṇā | upādānarthena upādānam | punarbhavajananārthena bhavaḥ | skandhaprādurbhāvārthena jātiḥ | skandhaparipākārthena jarā | vināśā

children.text: ) maraṇam | śocanārthena śokaḥ | vacanaparidevanārthena paridevaḥ | kāyasaṃpīḍanārthena duḥkham | cittasaṃpīḍanārthena daurmanasyam | upakleśārthena upāyāsāḥ ||

body.translated_text: Therein: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) has the meaning of great darkness. <s>Saṃskāras</s> (formations) have the meaning of fashioning. <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) has the meaning of cognizing. <s>Nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) has the meaning of mutual support. <s>Ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases) has the meaning of being gateways of approach. <s>Sparśa</s> (contact) has the meaning of touching. <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) has the meaning of experiencing. <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) has the meaning of intense thirst. <s>Upādāna</s> (clinging) has the meaning of grasping. <s>Bhava</s> (becoming) has the meaning of generating renewed existence. <s>Jāti</s> (birth) has the meaning of the manifestation of the aggregates. <s>Jarā</s> (aging) has the meaning of the maturation of the aggregates. Destruction —

body.text: punaraparam - tattve 'pratipattirmithyāpratipattirajñānamavidyā | evamavidyāyāṃ satyāṃ trividhāḥ saṃskārā abhinirvartante - puṇyopagā apuṇyopagā āneñjyopagāḥ | tatra puṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ puṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | apuṇyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmapuṇyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | āneñjyopagānāṃ saṃskārāṇāmāneñjyopagameva vijñānaṃ bhavati | idamucyate saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānamiti | vijñānasahabhuvaścatvāro 'rūpiṇaḥ skandhā nāmarūpam | tadvijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpamucyate | nāmarūpavivṛddhyā ṣaḍbhirāyatanadvāraiḥ kṛtyakriyāḥ pravartante | tannāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamityucyate | ṣaḍbhyaścāyatanebhyaḥ ṣaṭ sparśakāyāḥ pravartante | ayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśa ityucyate | yajjātīyaḥ sparśo bhavati, tajjātīyā vedanā pravartate | iyamucyate sparśapratyayā vedaneti | yastāṃ vedanāṃ viśeṣeṇāsvādayati abhinandati adhyavasyati adhyavasāya tiṣṭhati, sā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇetyucyate | āsvādanābhinandanādhyavasānādhyavasāyasthānādātmapriyarūpasātarūpairviyogo mā bhūditi nityamaparityāgāya yaivaṃ prārthanā, idamucyate tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam | evaṃ prārthayamānaḥ punarbhavajanakaṃ karma samutthāpayati kāyena vācā manasā ca, sa upādānapratyayo bhava ityucyate | tatkarmanirjātānāṃ pañcaskandhānāmabhinirvṛttiryā, sā bhavapratyayā jātirityucyate | jātyābhinirvṛttānāṃ skandhānāmupacayanaparipākādvināśo bhavati, tadidaṃ jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamityucyate ||

evamayaṃ dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ anyonyahetukaḥ anyonyapratyayaḥ | na nityo nānityo na saṃskṛto nāsaṃskṛto nāhetuko nāpratyayo na vedayitā na kṣayadharmo na vināśadharmo na nirodhadharmo 'nādikālapravṛtto 'nucchinno 'pravartate nadīsrotavat ||

yadyayaṃ dvādaśāṅgaḥ pratītyasamutpādo 'nyonyahetuko 'nyonyapratyayaḥ, na nityo nānityo na saṃskṛto nāsaṃskṛto nāhetuko nāpratyayo na vedayitā na kṣayadharmo na vināśadharmo na nirodhadharmo 'nādikālapravṛtto 'nucchinno 'nupravartate nadīsrotavat, atha ca imānyasya dvādaśāṅgasya pratītyasamutpādasya catvāri aṅgāni saṃghātakriyāyai hetutvena pravartante | katamāni catvāri? yaduta avidyā tṛṣṇā karma vijñānaṃ ca | tatra vijñānaṃ bījasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | karma kṣetrasvabhāvena hetuḥ | avidyā tṛṣṇā ca kleśasvabhāvatvena hetuḥ | tatra karmakleśā vijñānabījaṃ janayanti | tatra karma vijñānabījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karoti | tṛṣṇā vijñānabījaṃ snehayati | avidyā vijñānabījamavakirati | asatāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ vijñānabījasyābhinirvṛttirna bhavati | tatra karmaṇo naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ vijñānabījasya kṣetrakāryaṃ karomīti | tṛṣṇāyā api naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ vijñānabījaṃ snehayāmīti | avidyāyā api naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ vijñānabījamavakirāmīti | vijñānabījasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanitamiti | atha ca vijñānabījaṃ karmakṣetrapratiṣṭhitaṃ tṛṣṇāsnehābhiṣyanditamavidyayā svavakīrṇaṃ virohati | tatratatra upapattyāyatanapratisaṃdhau mātuḥkukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati | sa ca nāmarūpāṅkuro na svayaṃkṛto na parakṛto nobhayakṛto (

children.text:
) neśvarakṛto na kālapariṇāmito na prakṛtisaṃbhūto na caikakāraṇādhīno nāpyahetusamutpannaḥ | atha ca mātāpitṛsaṃyogadṛtusamavāyādanyeṣāṃ ca pratyayānāṃ samavāyāt tatra tatra āsvādaviddhaṃ vijñānabījamupapattyāyatanapratisaṃghau mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati, asvāmikeṣu dharmeṣu amameṣu aparigraheṣu ākāśasameṣu māyālakṣaṇasvabhāveṣu hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | tadyathā - pañcabhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ cakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? yaduta cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ ca ālokaṃ ca ākāśaṃ ca tajjamanasikāraṃ ca pratītya utpadyate cakṣurvijñānam | tatra cakṣurvijñānasya cakṣurāśrayakṛtyaṃ karoti | rūpaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya ālambanakṛtyaṃ karoti | ālokaḥ avabhāsakṛtyaṃ karoti | ākāśamanāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karoti | tajjamanasikāraḥ samanvāhārakṛtyaṃ
karoti | asatāmeṣāṃ pratyayānāṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ notpadyate | yadā tu cakṣurādhyātmikamāyatanamavikalaṃ bhavati, evaṃ rūpālokākāśatajjamanasikārāśca avikalā bhavanti, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ samavāyāccakṣurvijñānamutpadyate | tatra cakṣuṣo naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasyāśrayakṛtyaṃ karomīti | rūpasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya ālambanakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ālokasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya avabhāsakṛtyaṃ karomīti | ākāśasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya anāvaraṇakṛtyaṃ karomīti | tajjamanasikārasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya samanvāhārakṛtyaṃ karomīti | cakṣurvijñānasyāpi naivaṃ bhavati - ahamebhiḥ pratyayairjanitamiti | atha ca punaḥ satsu eṣu pratyayeṣu cakṣurvijñānasyotpattirbhavati | evaṃ śeṣāṇāmindriyāṇāṃ yathāyogaṃ yojyam ||
children.translated_text: ) not made by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), not transformed by time, not produced from <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), not dependent on a single cause, nor arisen without cause. And yet, from the conjunction of mother and father, from the confluence of the season and of other conditions, the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed, pierced by craving for flavor, at the rebirth-linking in the realm of a new existence, in the mother's womb, produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) — in <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, without 'mine,' without grasping, like space, of the nature of magical illusion — because of the completeness of causes and conditions. For example, visual consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>) arises from five causes. Which five? Namely, dependent on the eye, form, light, space, and the appropriate mental attention (<s>tajjamanasikāra</s>), visual consciousness arises. Therein, the eye performs the function of support for visual consciousness. Form performs the function of object (<s>ālambana</s>) for visual consciousness. Light performs the function of illumination. Space performs the function of non-obstruction. The appropriate mental attention performs the function of directing [the mind]. When these conditions are absent, visual consciousness does not arise. But when the eye as internal sense-base is complete, and likewise form, light, space, and the appropriate mental attention are complete, then from the coming together of all of them, visual consciousness arises. Therein, the eye does not think: 'I perform the function of support for visual consciousness.' Form also does not think: 'I perform the function of object for visual consciousness.' Light also does not think: 'I perform the function of illumination for visual consciousness.' Space also does not think: 'I perform the function of non-obstruction for visual consciousness.' The appropriate mental attention also does not think: 'I perform the function of directing visual consciousness.' Visual consciousness also does not think: 'I am generated by these conditions.' And yet, when these conditions are present, the arising of visual consciousness occurs. The same should be applied in due order to the remaining sense-faculties.

body.translated_text: If this twelve-linked <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) has mutual causation and mutual conditionality, is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither conditioned nor unconditioned, neither without cause nor without condition, neither experienced [by a self] nor subject to decay, nor subject to destruction, nor subject to cessation, has been operating since beginningless time, is uninterrupted, and continues like the current of a river — then there are four factors of this twelve-linked <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> that function as causes for the activity of aggregation. Which four? Namely: <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). Therein, <s>vijñāna</s> is a cause by virtue of being the nature of a seed. <s>Karma</s> is a cause by virtue of being the nature of a field. <s>Avidyā</s> and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> are causes by virtue of being the nature of defilements (<s>kleśa</s>). Therein, <s>karma</s> and the <s>kleśas</s> generate the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed. <s>Karma</s> performs the field-function for the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed. <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> moistens the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed. <s>Avidyā</s> scatters the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed. When these conditions are absent, the arising of the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed does not occur. Therein, <s>karma</s> does not think: 'I perform the field-function for the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed.' <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> also does not think: 'I moisten the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed.' <s>Avidyā</s> also does not think: 'I scatter the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed.' The <s>vijñāna</s>-seed also does not think: 'I am generated by these conditions.' And yet the <s>vijñāna</s>-seed, established in the field of <s>karma</s>, saturated with the moisture of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, scattered by <s>avidyā</s>, sprouts. At the rebirth-linking in the realm of a new existence, in the mother's womb, it produces the sprout of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form). And that <s>nāmarūpa</s>-sprout is not self-made, not other-made, not made by both,

body.text: tatra na kaściddharmo 'smāllokāt paralokaṃ saṃkrāmati | asti ca karmaphalaprativijñaptiḥ, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | tadyathā supariśuddhe ādarśamaṇḍale mukhapratibimbakaṃ dṛśyate | na ca tatra ādarśamaṇḍale mukhaṃ saṃkrāmati | asti ca mukhaprativijñaptiḥ, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | evamasmāllokāt na kaścit cyutaḥ, nāpyanyatropapannaḥ | asti ca karmaphalaprativijñaptiḥ, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | tadyathā candramaṇḍalaṃ catvāriṃśadyojanaśatamūrdhvaṃ vrajati | atha ca punaḥ parītte 'bhyudakabhājane candrasya pratibimbaṃ dṛśyate | na ca candramaṇḍalaṃ tasmātsthānāccyutam, parītte udakasya bhājane saṃkrāntaṃ bhavati | asti ca candramaṇḍalaprativijñaptiḥ, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | evamasmāllokānna kaścit cyutaḥ, nāpyanyatropapannaḥ | asti ca karmaphalaprativijñaptiḥ, hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt ||
body.translated_text: Therein, no <s>dharma</s> (entity) whatsoever transmigrates from this world to the next world. Yet there is the cognition of the fruits of <s>karma</s> (action), because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Just as in a well-polished mirror-surface, the reflection of a face is seen — yet the face does not transmigrate into the mirror-surface, and yet there is the cognition of the face due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions — so too, no one has departed from this world, nor has anyone been reborn elsewhere. Yet there is the cognition of the fruits of <s>karma</s>, because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Just as the disc of the moon travels forty thousand <s>yojanas</s> above, yet its reflection is seen even in a small vessel of water — and the moon-disc has not departed from that place, nor has it transmigrated into the small vessel of water, yet there is the cognition of the moon-disc due to the non-deficiency of causes and conditions — so too, no one has departed from this world, nor has anyone been reborn elsewhere. Yet there is the cognition of the fruits of <s>karma</s>, because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions.

body.text: tadyathā agnirupādānapratyaye sati jvalati, upādānavaikalyānna jvalati, evameva karmakleśajanitaṃ vijñānabījaṃ tatra tatra upapattyāyatanapratisaṃghau mātuḥ kukṣau nāmarūpāṅkuramabhinirvartayati, asvāmikeṣu dharmeṣu amameṣu aparigraheṣu ākāśasameṣu māyālakṣaṇasvabhāveṣu hetupratyayānāmavaikalyāt | evaṃ ādhyātmikasya pratītyasamutpādasya pratyayopanibandho draṣṭavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just as fire blazes when the condition of fuel is present, and does not blaze when fuel is lacking — so too, the seed of consciousness (<s>vijñānabīja</s>), born of <s>karma</s> and afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), produces the sprout of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) in the mother's womb in the appropriate realm of rebirth — among <s>dharmas</s> that are ownerless, without 'mine,' without possession, equal to space, and whose nature bears the character of illusion — because of the non-deficiency of causes and conditions. Thus should the dependence on conditions of the internal dependent origination be understood.

body.text: tatra ādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhirākārairdraṣṭavyaḥ | katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ? na śāśvatataḥ, nocchedataḥ, na saṃkrāntitaḥ, parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttataḥ, tatsadṛśānuprabandhataśceti | kathaṃ na śāśvatataḥ? yasmādanye māraṇāntikāḥ skandhāḥ, anye aupapattyaṃ

children.text: ) skandhāḥ, na tu ya evaṃ māraṇāntikāḥ skandhāḥ, ta eva aupapattyaṃśikāḥ | api tu māraṇāntikāḥ skandhā nirudhyante, tasminneva ca samaye aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti | ato na śāśvatataḥ || kathaṃ nocchedataḥ? na ca pūrvaniruddheṣu māraṇāntikeṣu skandheṣu aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti, nāpyaniruddheṣu | api tu māraṇāntikāḥ skandhā nirudhyante, tasminneva ca samaye aupapattyaṃśikāḥ skandhāḥ prādurbhavanti tulādaṇḍonnāmāvanāmavat | ato nocchedataḥ || kathaṃ na saṃkrāntitaḥ? visadṛśāḥ sattvanikāyāḥ sabhāgāyāṃ jātyāṃ jātimabhinirvartayanti | ato na saṃkrāntitaḥ | kathaṃ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ? parīttaṃ karma kriyate, vipulaḥ phalavipāko 'nubhūyate | ataḥ parīttahetuto vipulaphalābhinirvṛttitaḥ || kathaṃ tatsadṛśānuprabandhataḥ? yathāvedanīyaṃ karma kriyate, tathāvedanīyo vipāko 'nubhūyate | atastatsadṛśānuprabandhataśca || evamādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pañcabhirākārairdraṣṭavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) aggregates. It is not the case that the very aggregates at the time of death are themselves the aggregates at the time of rebirth. Rather, the aggregates at the time of death cease, and at that very moment the aggregates at the time of rebirth arise. Therefore, it is not from the standpoint of eternalism. How is it not from the standpoint of annihilationism? It is not the case that the aggregates at the time of rebirth arise when the aggregates at the time of death have previously ceased, nor when they have not yet ceased. Rather, the aggregates at the time of death cease, and at that very moment the aggregates at the time of rebirth arise — like the rising and falling of the beam of a balance. Therefore, it is not from the standpoint of annihilationism. How is it not from the standpoint of transmigration? Dissimilar classes of beings produce birth in a similar class of birth. Therefore, it is not from the standpoint of transmigration. How is it from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause? A small <s>karma</s> is performed, yet a vast fruit of ripening is experienced. Therefore, it is from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause. How is it from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the [cause]? Whatever type of <s>karma</s> is performed that is to be experienced [in a certain way], a corresponding type of ripening is experienced. Therefore, it is from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the cause. Thus should the internal dependent origination be viewed in five aspects.

body.translated_text: Therein, the internal dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) should be viewed in five aspects. Which five? Not from the standpoint of eternalism, not from the standpoint of annihilationism, not from the standpoint of transmigration, from the standpoint of a vast fruit arising from a small cause, and from the standpoint of a continuity similar to the [cause]. How is it not from the standpoint of eternalism? Because the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) at the time of death are different, and the aggregates at the time of rebirth are different —

body.text: yaḥ kaścid bhadanta śāriputra imaṃ pratītyasamutpādaṃ bhagavatā samyakpraṇītamevaṃ yathābhūtaṃ samyakprajñayā satatasamitamajīvaṃ nirjīvaṃ yathāvadaviparītamajātamabhūtamakṛtamasaṃskṛtamapratighamanālambaṃ śivamabhayamanāhāryamavyayamavyupaśamasvabhāvaṃ paśyati, asataḥ tucchataḥ riktataḥ asārataḥ rogataḥ gaṇḍataḥ śalyataḥ aghataḥ anityataḥ duḥkhataḥ śūnyataḥ anātmataḥ samanupaśyati, na sa pūrvāntaṃ pratisarati - kiṃ nvahamabhūvamatīte 'dhvani, kathaṃ nvahamabhūvamatīte 'dhvani iti | aparāntaṃ vā na punaḥ pratisarati - kiṃ nvahaṃ bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani, āhosvinna bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani, ko nu bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani, kathaṃ nu bhaviṣyāmyanāgate 'dhvani iti | pratyutpannaṃ vā punarnaṃ pratisarati - kiṃ nvidam, kathaṃ nvidam, ke santaḥ ke bhaviṣyāmaḥ, ime sattvāḥ kuta āgatāḥ, itaścyutāḥ kutra gamiṣyantīti | yāni ekeṣāṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇānāṃ pṛthag loke dṛṣṭigatāni bhaviṣyanti, tadyathā - ātmavādapratisaṃyuktāni sattvavādapratisaṃyuktāni jīvavādapratisaṃyuktāni pudgalavādapratisaṃyuktāni kautukamaṅgalavādapratisaṃyuktāni unmiñjitāni nimiñjitāni ca, tānyasya tasmin samaye prahīṇāni bhavanti parijñātāni samucchinnamūlāni tālamastakavadanābhāsagatāni āyatyāmanutpādānirodhadharmāṇi ||
body.translated_text: Whoever, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, sees this <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), rightly set forth by the Blessed One, as it truly is, with right wisdom — continuously and constantly, without life-force, without a soul, as it truly is, without error, unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, without obstruction, without support, quiescent, fearless, indestructible, imperishable, of the nature of cessation — and contemplates it as unreal, as empty, as hollow, as without essence, as disease, as a tumor, as a thorn, as misery, as impermanent, as suffering, as void (<s>śūnya</s>), as non-self (<s>anātman</s>) — he does not run toward the past [thinking]: 'Did I exist in the past? How did I exist in the past?' Nor does he run toward the future: 'Will I exist in the future? Will I not exist in the future? What will I be in the future? How will I be in the future?' Nor does he run toward the present: 'What is this? How is this? Being what, what shall we become? These beings — where have they come from, and having departed from here, where will they go?' Whatever views held by various <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> in the world — views connected with the doctrine of the self (<s>ātmavāda</s>), connected with the doctrine of being (<s>sattvavāda</s>), connected with the doctrine of a life-force (<s>jīvavāda</s>), connected with the doctrine of a person (<s>pudgalavāda</s>), connected with the doctrine of omens and auspicious signs (<s>kautukamaṅgalavāda</s>), and [views that are] stretched out and contracted — all of those, at that moment, are abandoned for him, fully understood, with their roots cut off, like a palmyra tree-top, brought to a state of non-existence, subject to non-arising and cessation in the future.

body.text: yo bhadanta śāriputra evaṃvidhadharmakṣāntisamanvitaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ samyagavagacchati, tasya tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavit puruṣadamyasārathiranattaraḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān samyaksaṃbodhiṃ vyākaroti - samyaksaṃbuddho buddho bhaviṣyasīti | maitreyeṇa bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evamuktam ||
body.translated_text: Whoever, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, possesses such patience regarding the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmakṣānti</s>) and rightly comprehends <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> — to him the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed Charioteer of Persons to be Tamed, the Teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, gives the prediction of perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>): 'You will become a perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>.' Thus spoke the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro maitreyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bhāṣitamabhinandya anupramodya utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ | prakrāntāste ca bhikṣavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, rejoicing in and approving of the words spoken by the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, rose from his seat and departed. And those <s>bhikṣus</s> departed.

body.text: āryaśālistambaṃ nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ saṃpūrṇam ||
body.translated_text: The Noble <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>Sūtra</s> called <s>Śālistamba</s> (The Rice Stalk) is complete.
